paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We measure the average similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models. We observe that the similarity score becomes lower as the size of S increases.

model_annotations.German: This plot illustrates the relationship between the size of subset S and the average cosine similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models, comparing two methods: Weight averaging and QAdapter. The x-axis, labeled "|S|", has a linear scale, ranging from 2 to 10 with a tick label interval of 2, and represents the size of subset S. The y-axis, labeled "Cosine similarity", also has a linear scale, ranging from 0.1 to 0.5 with a tick label interval of 0.1 (implied by values 0.1, 0.3, 0.5), and represents the cosine similarity between the models. The blue dashed line with square markers represents Weight averaging, starting at approximately 0.48 when |S| is 2 and decreasing to around 0.32 when |S| is 10, with a steady decline across the x-axis. The green dashed line with circular markers represents QAdapter, starting at around 0.38 when |S| is 2 and decreasing to approximately 0.2 when |S| is 10, also showing a steady decline.
